articles.title: Hisar Integrated Manufacturing Cluster To Drive Rs 32,417 Cr Investment, 1.25 Lakh Jobs
articles.description: Hisar Integrated Manufacturing Cluster To Drive Rs 32,417 Cr Investment, 1.25 Lakh Jobs Chandigarh, Sep 18 (KNN) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini has directed officials to expedite construction of the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) near Maharaja Agrasen International Airport in Hisar, a project with an estimated investment potential of Rs 32,417 crore and employment potential of around 1.25 lakh jobs. The directions were issued during a review of major development projects under the State Pragati Portal, where officials briefed the Chief Minister on the progress of the IMC and associated airport infrastructure. First Phase Covers 1,578 Acres The first phase of the IMC covers 1,578 acres, with the government having acquired 100 per cent of the required land. Environmental clearance has also been secured. The construction tender has been floated and the evaluation and selection of bids are at an advanced stage, following which work is expected to begin. The overall IMC will span 2,988 acres at an estimated project cost of Rs 4,680 crore. Multi-Sector Industrial Hub The cluster is planned as a multi-sector industrial hub covering defence and aerospace, agro-food processing, garments and textiles, along with supporting infrastructure. The development will also include a Skill Development Centre, Convention Centre and Exhibition Hall, Logistics Park and Multi-Speciality Hospital. Saini directed officials to make provisions for aerospace, an Army corridor and medical activities within the cluster, while also reviewing requirements for Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) operations at Hisar Airport. Airport, Logistics Infrastructure Infrastructure linked to the airport is being developed alongside the cluster, including water supply facilities and a 220-kV power substation to support upcoming industrial and commercial facilities. The IMC is being developed under the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor in collaboration with the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC). Located near the airport and key road and rail networks, the cluster will have connectivity through NH-52 and NH-09 and proximity to the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors. Saini instructed officials to ensure that construction activities face no delays while maintaining quality standards. (KNN Bureau)

articles.title: DPIIT floats Rs 4 crore tender for social media management services
articles.description: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has invited bids to hire a social media agency for a two-year contract. The GeM tender, dated September 14, 2026, covers social media content creation, content response and moderation, campaign management, response management and helpdesk support, along with basic reporting and analytics. The agency will handle Hindi and English content across Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, WhatsApp, and YouTube. The estimated bid value is Rs 40 million, inclusive of all taxes. The minimum average annual turnover requirement for bidders is Rs 500 lakh, with at least five years of past experience in providing similar services. The tender requires bidders to have completed three major social media management projects for any state or central government, local body, or public sector undertaking. The bid will be evaluated under the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a 70:30 weighting for technical and financial components. Bidders must secure at least 70 marks in the technical evaluation. The scope also includes a fresh photoshoot for creating a photo bank and developing 1-2 minute video content through a fresh shoot. The agency is required for 24 months. The bid submission deadline is September 29, 2026, at 1 PM, with the bids scheduled to open on September 30 at 1 PM. The earnest money deposit is Rs 800,000, while the ePBG is set at 3%, with a required duration of 26 months.

articles.title: Maharashtra’s New Govt Lab to Train Workforce in Solar, Hydrogen and BESS
articles.description: The Maharashtra Energy Development Agency (MEDA) has floated a ₹90 lakh tender to establish a laboratory focused on green hydrogen, renewable energy and energy storage technologies at its head office in Pune, with the facility intended to provide hands-on training, demonstration and research exposure to students, engineers, industry personnel and government officials. Under the tender, the state agency has invited experienced vendors for the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of the laboratory setup. The estimated project cost is ₹90 lakh, excluding taxes. The tender carries an EMD of ₹1 lakh and a document fee of ₹11,800, including GST. The tender was published on September 10, 2026, with bids to be submitted by September 28 at 3 pm. The technical bids are scheduled to be opened on October 5 at 3 pm. Six technology platforms The proposed laboratory will bring together six separate training and research systems covering solar PV, wind, energy management, hydrogen and battery storage. These include a Solar PV Training and Research System, Solar PV Grid-Tied Training System, Wind Energy Training System, Renewable Energy-based Smart Energy Management System, Hydrogen Generation, Storage and Utilization System, and a Battery and BMS Learn-and-Build Platform. MEDA said the facility is being developed in line with the Maharashtra Green Hydrogen Policy 2023 and the Maharashtra Renewable Energy and Energy Storage Policy 2025-26 to 2035-36, which provide for skill-linked technical training and R&D capacity building in renewable energy and energy storage. The laboratory is intended to give engineers, students, industry personnel and MEDA officials practical exposure to solar PV systems, wind energy conversion, hybrid renewable energy management, hydrogen generation, storage and utilisation, and battery energy storage technologies. Solar systems to cover grid and off-grid applications The Solar PV Training and Research System will include PV modules, an artificial sunlight source, power conditioning equipment, battery storage, a DC-DC converter, inverter and data-logging capabilities. The system is designed to enable experiments involving PV I-V and P-V characteristics, maximum power point tracking (MPPT), standalone DC/AC loads, battery charging and discharging, the impact of tilt angle and shading, and PV power-flow calculations. A separate grid-tied training system will use a programmable solar PV emulator capable of reproducing the I-V/P-V characteristics of a solar array. It will also include a virtual grid, grid-tied inverter and power-quality equipment. The system will allow trainees to study grid synchronisation, power flows, net metering, power-factor improvement and anti-islanding protection. Hybrid renewable energy management The proposed smart energy management system will combine a minimum 2 kW solar PV array with a minimum 1 kW wind turbine and a 24 V, 100 Ah lithium-ion battery bank. It will include a weather station measuring solar irradiance, humidity, wind speed and direction, rainfall and temperature. A central control system will monitor the solar PV system, wind system, battery, inverters, AC mains and loads, with RS-485 communication and power-analysis capabilities. The training platform will allow users to study standalone and grid-connected solar operation, wind systems, solar-wind hybrid operation with batteries, smart-home energy monitoring and automatic switching between energy sources and loads. Hydrogen-to-power training system One of the key components will be an integrated hydrogen generation, storage and utilisation system. The proposed setup will use an alkaline electrolyser for hydrogen production, cylinder storage and a PEM fuel cell for electricity generation. The electrolyser is specified to produce up to 3,000 ml of hydrogen per minute, with hydrogen purity above 99.99%. The PEM fuel cell will have a rated power of at least 1 kW and will allow users to study hydrogen-to-electricity conversion, including voltage, current, power and efficiency characteristics. The system will also incorporate hydrogen leak detectors, automatic solenoid shut-off, non-return valves, dual-stage pressure regulation and alarm/interlock systems for over-pressure and leak conditions. Experiments will include operating the electrolyser, monitoring hydrogen generation and pressure, running the fuel cell using stored hydrogen and analysing energy losses across the hydrogen-to-electricity cycle. BESS and battery-management training MEDA is also proposing a dedicated Battery and BMS Learn-and-Build Platform, designed to provide hands-on exposure to battery management systems, battery cycling, protection functions and State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH) estimation. The platform will support battery configurations of up to 23S × 5P and be compatible with LiFePO4 chemistry. It will include individual cell-voltage monitoring, current and temperature measurement, passive balancing and protection against over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, short circuits and temperature extremes. The system will also feature a programmable battery cycler capable of charging and discharging batteries under constant-current, constant-power and C-rate modes. Its experiments will cover battery ageing, degradation, BMS algorithms and long-term data logging for research and reporting. Five-year warranty and training All six laboratory systems will come with a minimum five-year warranty from installation, with the tender requiring supply, installation, testing, commissioning, demonstration and training as part of the scope. The tender also requires relevant BIS, IEC, IS or ISO compliance where applicable, along with test and calibration certificates, user manuals, data acquisition and monitoring facilities, and communication interfaces such as RS-485, Modbus or Ethernet wherever applicable. For bidders, the tender sets a minimum average annual turnover requirement of ₹90 lakh over the previous three financial years. The bidder or its OEM must also have regularly manufactured and supplied the same or similar category of products to a Central or state government organisation, PSU or reputed university during the previous three financial years. The procurement could therefore create a specialised opportunity for renewable-energy training equipment suppliers, hydrogen technology companies and battery/BMS system providers, while giving MEDA a dedicated facility to build practical skills around technologies expected to play a larger role in Maharashtra's renewable-energy and energy-storage ecosystem.

articles.title: Meghalayan Age issues RFP for media and PR agency under MyMeG
articles.description: New Delhi: Meghalayan Age Limited (MAL) has issued a Request for Proposal to appoint a media and public relations agency for the Government of Meghalaya under its MyMeG programme. The RFP, dated September 17, 2026, seeks an agency to build the state's development narrative across regional, national and international media. The mandate puts a strong emphasis on earned media. The selected agency will be expected to secure regular authored features, bylines and editorial coverage in national print and digital publications, while also supporting government departments with press releases, media queries and day-to-day communications. The RFP specifically states that the approach should rely on credible editorial storytelling rather than advertorial or overtly promotional content. The communication agenda will cover areas including participatory governance, agriculture and market linkages, sustainable and concert tourism, sports and the National Games, infrastructure, urban development and investment promotion. Beyond media outreach, the agency will be responsible for continuous monitoring of local, regional and national media, rebuttals and clarifications, crisis and reputation support, media interactions and liaison with Khasi, Garo and Pnar-language media. Management of the government's official social media handles is outside the scope, although the agency may be required to provide content inputs. From the third month of the engagement, the RFP sets minimum targets including four authored or bylined articles in national publications each month, one national magazine feature, six placements on leading domestic news websites and 15 regional or local media placements. It also seeks at least two media interactions or briefings a month and a minimum of three press releases or statements a week. Eligible agencies must have been operating for at least 10 years and have earned at least Rs 10 crore annually from PR, media relations, content/editorial and digital media services in each of the last three financial years. They must also have serviced at least three government clients during the period and maintain operational offices in at least four major metropolitan cities, including Delhi-NCR and Mumbai. The selection will follow a quality-and-cost-based system, with technical and financial scores carrying an 80:20 weightage. Agencies need at least 70 technical marks to qualify for financial evaluation. The engagement will initially run for 12 months and can be extended for another 12 months based on performance. The RFP carries an earnest money deposit of Rs 5 lakh, while the selected agency will be required to furnish a performance bank guarantee equivalent to 5% of the annual contract value. The tender notice lists October 6 as the deadline for hard-copy submission, October 7 as the RFP closing date and October 9 as the deadline for submitting the technical proposal by email.

articles.title: Cornea Unveils AI-Driven Pro AV Innovations and Next-Gen Displays at InfoComm India 2026
articles.description: Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 18: Cornea, a prominent Indian Pro AV and display solutions manufacturer, successfully showcased its latest innovations at InfoComm India 2026, held from September 16 to 18 at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. The company demonstrated its expanded ecosystem under the central theme, “One Brand for Every Display Need,” highlighting its commitment to providing a single, comprehensive source for hardware, software, and AI-enabled AV infrastructure across education, corporate, government, and institutional sectors.
